draft.title: Types of pathogens
card: A pathogen is an agent that causes disease. The main types are prions, viruses, bacteria, protozoa, fungi and parasites.
Virus
a tiny particle of genetic material in a protein coat. It has no cell structure, so it can only reproduce inside a host cell, which it often damages or kills.
Bacteria
single-celled organisms that reproduce on their own. Some cause disease by damaging tissue or releasing toxins.
Prion
an abnormally folded protein with no genetic material. It causes disease by making normal proteins in the host fold the wrong way.
draft.remember: Pathogens differ in how they cause harm. Only viruses must reproduce inside a host cell.

a.q: Why can a virus not reproduce on a laboratory dish of nutrients alone?
opts: It has no cell structure and needs a host cell
It has no protein coat to hold its genes
It is a single cell that needs oxygen to divide
It is a misfolded protein that cannot copy itself
a.why: A virus has no cell structure of its own, so it relies on a host cell to reproduce. Bacteria are single cells that reproduce independently, so a nutrient dish can grow them but not viruses.
a.clue: Think about what a virus lacks that a cell has.

b.q: A disease in cattle is traced to an infectious agent with no DNA or RNA. It causes harm by making normal proteins in the brain fold abnormally. What is the agent most likely to be?
opts: A prion
A virus
A bacterium
A protozoan
b.why: Only a prion is an infectious protein with no genetic material, and it spreads damage by misfolding normal proteins. A virus is tempting because it is also tiny and not a cell, but it contains DNA or RNA.
b.clue: Which pathogen has no genetic material at all?

a.best: It has no cell structure and needs a host cell

problems.detail: 'Only viruses must reproduce inside a host cell' is false. Some bacteria, such as Chlamydia and Rickettsia, and some protozoa, such as Plasmodium, are obligate intracellular pathogens. Prions also only propagate inside a host. The card itself never claims this is unique to viruses.
The remember line uses 'only' and 'must', which overstate the card. Something like 'Viruses can only reproduce inside a host cell' would be accurate.

'Bacteria: single-celled organisms that reproduce on their own' overgeneralises, because obligate intracellular bacteria such as Chlamydia cannot. Adding 'most' would fix it. Why (a) repeats the same overgeneralisation when it says a nutrient dish can grow bacteria.

check.summary: Both questions are sound, but the remember line wrongly says only viruses must reproduce inside a host cell; some bacteria and protozoa, such as Chlamydia and Plasmodium, must too. The card's claim that bacteria reproduce on their own should also say 'most'.

proposal.title: Types of pathogens
card: A pathogen is an agent that causes disease. The main types are prions, viruses, bacteria, protozoa, fungi and parasites.
Virus
a tiny particle of genetic material (DNA or RNA) in a protein coat. It has no cell structure, so it can only reproduce inside a host cell, which it often damages or kills.
Bacteria
single-celled organisms with their own DNA, and most can reproduce on their own. Protozoa and fungi are also living cells with DNA. Some bacteria cause disease by damaging tissue or releasing toxins.
